summary: Mary McGee is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts as Associate Professor at Columbia University (attested 1996–1998), Chair at Dartmouth College (attested 1998), and Dean and Professor of Religious Studies at Alfred University (attested 2013).

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. She studied at the University of Michigan, Columbia University (PhD), NYU, and Harvard. Her career included posts at the U.S. Department of State and the National Museum of African Art.
Marybeth White works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a double major honors degree at York University and pursued doctoral studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Stanisław Schayer (~1932–1939). She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1937–1939) and was a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society (1974).
Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She held a professorship at Smith College (attested 1986).

Marzenna Jakubczak is a philosopher and Indologist who earned her PhD at Jagiellonian University (1992–1998) and completed her habilitation at Maria Curie-Skłodowska University (2013–2014). She taught at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and became Associate Professor at Jagiellonian University in 2024.

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. Educated at Kyoto University (~1949–1980, Litt.D.), he served on Kyoto University's staff and faculty (1968; 1981–1993) before becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori (b. 1924) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta (D.Phil.) and held major academic posts at Kyoto University (1961–1988) and Hanazono University (~1992–1998).

Masaaki Nitta (b. 1936) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He served as an associate professor (attested 2003) and later professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.

Masaaki Sugiyama (1952–2019) was a historian, sinologist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1979) and held an academic post at Kyoto Women's University (~1989–1992).
Masaaki Tsuchiya (b. 1960) is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University and held a post at Senshu University around 2000.

Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University under scholars including Deussen and Oldenberg, he was a longtime professor and library director at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai (b. 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. After earning his doctorate at Tokyo University of Education, he held posts at Ibaraki University and the University of Tsukuba, later directing the Shinshu Cultural Center.

Masahide Mori (b. 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and the University of London (PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski) and held faculty positions at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, and Kanazawa University.
Masahide Tsujimura is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Kyoto University and served as an Assistant Professor at Kobe University in 2013.
Masahiro Asada (b. 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and served there as an associate professor from approximately 1984 to 1990.

Masahiro Inami (b. 1960) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University (~1985–1990) and held academic posts at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1996, ~2008).

Masahiro Kusunoki (1921–2009) was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1948–1953) and later served there as chair professor of the history of religions (~1969–1985).

Masahiro Shimoda (b. 1957) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Delhi, and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and joined Musashino University in 2023.
